title: Annotatio III §.XI (7): Scripture backs multi-sense testimony — reading/hearing; Reason’s empire over senses
pass_a_gloss: Revealed Holy Scripture itself declares in more than one way (1) by recommending itself to our senses, i.e. to Reading and Hearing — which it would do rashly if faith is not to be had in the senses. (2) by deferring empire over the Senses to Reason, especially illuminated, and circumscribing it with certain limits — on which it would lean in vain if the acts of the Senses are fallible.
pass_b_english: Revealed Scripture itself backs that: (1) it trusts itself to our senses in reading and hearing — rash if senses deserve no faith.
(2) it gives Reason empire over the senses within limits — pointless if sense-acts are fallible.
source_text: Ipsa revelata Scriptura S. non unô modô edicit (1) Semet ipsam sensibus nostris, i. e. Lectioni & Auditioni commendando, id quod temere faceret, si sensibus fides habenda non sit. (2) Imperium in Sensus Rationi, præsertim illuminatæ, deferendo certisque limitibus circumscrivendo, in quod frustra niteretur, si Sensuum actus fallibiles sint.
